title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 87
paragraphs: So, as the ravages did not cease, on the twentieth day Timagenides spoke as follows to the Thebans: “Thebans, since the Greeks have resolved not to abandon the siege until either they have taken Thebes or you have delivered us up to them, let the land of Boeotia no longer suffer on our account. If they desire money and are demanding our surrender as a pretext for this, let us give them money taken out of the state's treasury — for we took the Medes' side together with the state, not by ourselves alone; but if they are truly conducting the siege to get us into their hands, then we will give ourselves up for trial.” It was thought that he spoke well and at the right time, and the Thebans at once sent a herald to Pausanias offering to hand over the men.
